reason: E2 supports the premise that Al2O3 is an excellent oxygen barrier, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that a pre-oxidation treatment of NbTaTiAlV forms a coherent, adherent alumina-rich layer or that such a layer remains effective under the specified conditions. E1 actually shows that Al2O3 was not continuous and not protective in a related alloy, which undermines the feasibility claim.
premises: Al2O3 is an excellent barrier to oxygen diffusion at high temperatures
Pre-oxidation at 800°C in low pO2 can form a coherent, adherent alumina-rich layer on NbTaTiAlV
A continuous Al2O3 layer reduces oxidation kinetics and weight gain
Untreated NbTaTiAlV forms a less uniform, less protective oxide scale
The pre-formed Al2O3 layer remains stable and effective during 1000°C air exposure for 100 hours
